title: Homily LXXXII
subtitle: Matthew 26:26-28
author: chrysostom
excerpt: Ah! how great is the blindness of the traitor! Even partaking of the mysteries, he remained the same; and admitted to the most holytable, he changed not. And…

footnotes.1: [εχαριστσα (from verse 27) is substituted for ελογσα; and ἔδωκεν (from the same verse) for ἐδδου (rec. text) or δος, of the more ancient authorities.—R.]
footnotes.2: [The text agrees exactly with the received; except in the substitution of ὑπρ for περ. The R.V. following the older authorities, omits “new,” also rendering διαθκη “covenant” in the text.—R.]
footnotes.3: [φρικωδεσττη, “most awful;” literally, “most terrifying,” but applied to religious awe.—R.]
footnotes.4: Luke xxii. 3; see also John xiii. 27.
footnotes.6: See 1 Cor. xi. 26, and St. Chrys. on the place, Hom. XXVII. on 1 Cor., where he attributes the words “until He come,” expressly to St. Paul. Various early writers attribute them to our Lord.
footnotes.9: Matt. xxvi. 29. [The word “henceforth” is omitted; “this” is joined with “vine,” and “new” is in a different position in the Greek. All these are variations from the received text, which is also followed in the R.V.—R.]
footnotes.12: See Zech. xiii. 7. [The words “of the flock” are omitted, as in Mark xiv. 27. They do not occur in the passage in Zechariah.—R.]
footnotes.15: Matt. xxvi. 33. [The word ἀλλ is inserted, as in Mark xiv. 29.—R.]
footnotes.19: Luke xxii. 31. [R.V., “Satan asked;” margin, “Or, obtained you by asking.”]
footnotes.20: [The preposition ἐν is omitted from the Greek text.—R.]
footnotes.21: Matt. xxvi. 34, 35. [R.V., “If I must die with thee, yet will I not deny thee.”]
footnotes.34: Heb. x. 29. [Slightly altered, as in Homily LXXV. 5, p. 455.—R.]
